Actually there are 5 written methods:

Katakana : very angular and simple used for loan words like hamburger

Hiragana : curvy and simple used for children's books, grammar functions and in conjunction with Kanji

Kanji : Chinese characters, can be used as a main word which normally read with Chinese based readings. The other method is in conjunction with hiragana which will almost always be read with Japanese readings.

The last 2 are actually one but are the easier for us. They are 2 ways to convert Japanese sounds into roman characters known to us as the ABCs.

The Japanese Kanji are older forms of the Chinese characters. Chinese is all characters which makes it seem harder to read but from what I've heard it's easier because you'll only see that combinations in one form not like Japanese or English (think here of the words take and get and their combinations).

So ... To your question. Yes and No. Over all I'd say that a majority are used similar if you consider just a single character instance and No if you consider that new combinations and a slight variety occurred when the Japanese introduced this writing method to Japan.

Korea does use Chonese characters too but mostly in literature and newspapers. However, Hangul was only inspired by Chinese characters and was created by a mathematician.
